key_insight: Free-surface effects in turbulent open-channel flow are transported mainly by pressure-related and viscous transport terms, and they couple near-wall scales with outer-layer very-large-scale motions rather than following one universal scaling.
engineering_relevance: For open-channel and hydraulic design, this means surface-driven momentum and energy exchange can influence near-surface mixing, turbulence models, and boundary-condition assumptions across multiple scales.
method: Matched open- and closed-channel DNS up to Re_tau ≈ 900
Compared turbulent kinetic energy budget terms near the free surface
Examined pressure-strain redistribution and scale organization using VLSM-resolving domains
evidence_signal: The analysis uses direct numerical simulations with matched configurations and a domain large enough to capture very-large-scale motions, enabling term-by-term comparison of near-surface TKE budgets.
watch_item: The reported near-surface scaling is not universal, so applying a single wall-law or one-scale surface model may miss Reynolds-number-dependent and outer-layer coupling effects.
paper_title: How is the free surface influence transported in turbulent open channel flows?
